title: Joint Pre-training and Local Re-training: Transferable Representation Learning on Multi-source Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: Different knowledge graphs contain complementary information that could improve knowledge graph embeddings and downstream tasks.

contributions.claim: A joint pre-training and local re-training framework is proposed for learning and applying multi-source knowledge graph embeddings.
The framework pre-trains a teacher embedding model over linked multi-source knowledge graphs and distills knowledge to a student model for a task-specific knowledge graph.
The framework uses entity alignment and three-level knowledge distillation comprising feature, network, and prediction knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge across knowledge graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating the effectiveness and efficiency of the framework.
The authors report that the teacher model can be reused for different target knowledge graphs and tasks without training from scratch.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work is motivated by complementary information across knowledge graphs that may improve embeddings and downstream tasks.
The paper presents a joint pre-training and local re-training framework using a teacher model trained over linked multi-source knowledge graphs and a student model for a task-specific graph.
Entity alignment creates a linked subgraph, which is re-trained using feature, network, and prediction knowledge distillation.
The authors report teacher-model reuse across target graphs and tasks and experiments on effectiveness and efficiency.

unknowns: The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not specify the entity-alignment procedure or the training objectives for the three distillation levels.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness, efficiency, or reuse claims.
